newsitem.title: GERMANY: German shares draw breath, but outlook stable.
newsitem.headline: German shares draw breath, but outlook stable.

text.p: German shares weakened in early pre-bourse trade on Tuesday, taking a break after the DAX index breached the psychologically key 4,000 point level on Monday, but the outlook was for stable trade, dealers said.

With the dollar still firm and little expected in the way of surprising economic or corporate news, dealers said the blue chip index had every chance of hovering close to its record highs though the day.
Early selective buying interest focused on Bayerische Motoren Werke AG, but the carmaker described as nonsense talk that it planned to sell its Rover small car unit.
BMW hit an early high of 1,505 marks on the talk, but then fell back to trade up 13.35 marks at 1,490 marks at 0724 marks.
British press reports had on Monday said Chrysler Corp had shown interest in buying BMW's Rover small car unit.
The IBIS DAX index, which tracks electronic trade, was down 10.33 points at 3,993.02 points.
"I don't think anyone believed we would hold above 4,000 points at the very start but there is no reason why we can't get back there in the bourse session," said a Frankfurt dealer.
"This is just a bit of a breather. There is no serious selling pressure," he added.

Electronics and engineering giant Siemens AG was also higher, trading up 50 pfennigs at 109.50 marks, as talk circulated on the chance that GEC may be poised to pull out of GPT, a telecommunications joint venture between Siemens and GEC Alsthom.
"People are saying Siemens could take a larger role in the unit, and that's got some buyers interested," a Frankfurt dealer said.
GEC said on Tuesday that it was reviewing GPT's role with Siemens.
The German jobs report was having minimal impact.

The seasonally adjusted jobless number rose 11,000 in June from May, indicating ongoing problems on the German labour market and supporting expectations for continued low interest rates in the country.
